reasons: Case exists and is correctly identified: cached opinion header '532 U.S. 318 (2001)', 'ATWATER et al. v. CITY OF LAGO VISTA et al.', 'Decided April 24, 2001', Souter, J. — matches.
'official_citation_present:false' is belied by the record's own '532 U.S. 318' type-1 cite; same selector bug as al-Kidd (both list 'Fla. L. Weekly Fed. S').

Cached opinion: 'The question is whether the Fourth Amendment forbids a warrantless arrest for a minor criminal offense, such as a misdemeanor seatbelt violation punishable only by a fine. We hold that it does not.'

Star page *354: 'the standard of probable cause applie[s] to all arrests, without the need to balance... If an officer has probable cause to believe that an individual has committed even a very minor criminal offense in his presence, he may, without violating the Fourth Amendment, arrest the offender' — confirms both the fine-only-misdemeanor holding and the no-individualized-balancing rule.

Atwater establishes authority to make a full custodial arrest for a minor/fine-only offense — the lawful-custodial-arrest predicate that triggers a search incident to arrest of the person; a cross-doctrine link to SIA Persons is grounded.

Atwater is the anchor SCOTUS authority on warrantless custodial arrest for a fine-only/minor offense on probable cause; 'Key — Anchor (minor-offense custodial arrest on probable cause)' on Arrest and Arrest Warrants is squarely supported by the holding and the *354 passage.

A custodial arrest is a Fourth Amendment seizure of the person (Atwater alleged violation of the 'right to be free from unreasonable seizure'); its reasonableness holding bears on Seizure of the Person as a cross-doctrine reference.
2001 SCOTUS categorical arrest rule, never overruled and expressly extended by Virginia v. Moore (2008) as the scope_note states.

Negative edges are proposed:true triage (e.g., Commonwealth v. Buckley 'superseded_by_statute' — a state statute limiting arrest authority, which Atwater itself contemplated at *352); none is an overruling of Atwater's constitutional holding.
Cached opinion: 'Souter, J., delivered the opinion of the Court' (5-4) — a SCOTUS majority; 'Binding — SCOTUS' correct.
